get.summary: Every comment left on one asset within one version, oldest first
The current guest's favorited asset keys within one version

N-02: `from`/`to` narrow this to a date range — the query "which
     * shoots fall in March" — on top of I-02's plain `since` staleness
filter, which the shared page() below still applies. Both bounds are
inclusive and optional independently, so a caller can ask for
everything from a date onward, or up to one, as well as a closed range

N-02: the single-resource read the index alone can't answer — "get a
     * project" needs the project, not a page that might contain it. Route
model binding does the tenant + public_id lookup (and the 404 for a
project outside the token's tenant) the same as every other
`{project:public_id}` route on this surface already does

N-02: the funnel, not the leads that make it up — a count per
stage rather than a page of Lead rows the caller would have to
tally itself. Same grouping order as LeadBoardController's own board
(declaration order, not the stored strings' alphabetical order) and
the same `open()` scope: a lost lead left its stage the moment it was
marked lost, so it no longer belongs to any column's count

parameters.name: preview
parameters.description:
is_string(), not a raw query('preview'): a ?preview[]=x arrives as an
 array, and opens(?string) exploding one would fatal into a 500 — the
 uniform-failure rule this stage worked to establish. Treated the same
 as no token at all, not coerced (PHP's array-to-string cast raises a
 warning PHPUnit's own handler turns back into a fatal).

elapsed.description:
Seconds since the page rendered, computed server-side by
apps/gallery from a hidden timestamp field (this page ships
no client JavaScript, so there is no inline script to send

for the same reason theirs is: a first-ever render has

parameters.description:

 beats that gallery's public default. is_string(), not a raw
 query('preview'): see GalleryDraftImageController's own comment

post.description:
One transaction, for the reason CommitHistoricalImport gives: a run
that wrote 140 rows and refused the 141st leaves nothing to tell the
imported rows from the ones that never landed, and a second attempt
duplicates whatever the first one kept.

Rows are validated one at a time rather than through one `leads.*`
rule set: contact_name is `required_without:contact_id`, and under a
wildcard that reference resolves against the top level, never the
sibling in the same row.

Every row is checked before the first one is written, because the
transaction only takes back the database: CaptureInquiry dispatches
LeadCaptured, the studio's mail about it is out of the building
immediately, and a rollback cannot recall it. Refusing the batch
before anything is captured is what keeps that mail from naming a
lead nobody can open.

entered_at.description:
Since when it stands there, for a move entered after the fact. A
stage below the current one is a correction and takes back the
booking with it — see AdvanceLeadStage.

consent.description:
T-02's Datenschutz link is shown beside this box; refusing
without it is the one validation error this endpoint is willing
to report, because it is a fact about the submission rather
than about the studio's data.

Seconds since the form rendered, written by the snippet's own
inline script. Optional: a client with no JavaScript still gets
to send an inquiry.

202.description:
No id, no name, nothing to correlate. The client is told the
studio has it; anything more is a fact the internet does not need.

Mirrors App\Crm\Http\Controllers\ShootController::store: the same
rules, the same nullable date, and the model's own defaults for status,
is_primary and sort_order — the primary one is already taken.
post.summary:
A second shooting day on a project that already has one. CaptureInquiry
makes exactly one shoot and marks it primary; a wedding split over two
days — Trauung on one, Feier on another — has no way to reach the
second from here otherwise

CaptureChannel.description: How the inquiry reached the studio — a different question from LeadSource, which is how the client heard about it. A referral can arrive by phone or by mail, and neither fact can be recovered afterwards, so both are stored.
CaptureChannel.title: CaptureChannel

CaptureInquiryData.description:
The capture form's payload. Six fields the studio fills plus the contact
block, matching mockup 03 — venue, guest count, further shoots and package
are deliberately absent and belong to the project screen.

No #[TypeScript]: this is request input, and the frontend builds it rather
than receiving it.

contact_id.description:
The CUID2 of an existing contact, or a name for a new one. One
of the two is required; both together simply reuse the contact.

date.description:
Nullable and never checked against existing bookings. The
availability warning is advisory by design — see
CheckDateAvailability.

captured_at.description:
A day, a moment, or nothing. Never the future: an inquiry that
has not arrived yet is a typo, and it would sit at the head of
every funnel month until someone found it.

referred_by_contact_id.description:
The CUID2 of an existing contact, same shape as contact_id
above. Nullable always, including when the source is a
referral — see the migration.

CaptureInquiryData.title: CaptureInquiryData

LeadOutcome.description: How a pursuit ended. `lost_at` carried only "not booked" and left the why in free text; T-20's scan needs to tell a finished inquiry from a waiting one, and a client who cancelled from one the studio turned away. Null is open, and open is the only state the stalled scan reminds about.
LeadOutcome.title: LeadOutcome

LeadSource.description: How the client heard about the studio. A fixed list rather than free text: it is the one fact that cannot be read back out of the inquiry text later, and its entire value is being countable (mockup 03).
LeadSource.title: LeadSource

ProjectFieldType.description: C-25: what a studio may ask of a project of one type. Deliberately not FormFieldType — the questionnaire knows files, name lists and group photos, a project field does not, and the two vocabularies are meant to grow apart.
ProjectFieldType.title: ProjectFieldType

ShootKind.description: What kind of occasion a shoot is. Finer-grained than ProjectType: one wedding project routinely holds an engagement shoot, the wedding day and the reception, separated by as much as a year.
ShootKind.title: ShootKind

errors.description: A detailed description of each field that failed validation.
